items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Amara wanted to plant a sunflower. She dug a small hole, dropped in the seed, and watered it every day. Two weeks later, a tiny green sprout poked through the soil. By summer the sunflower was taller than Amara herself.

Describe the beginning, middle, and end of this story in one sentence each.
items.answer: Beginning: Amara plants a sunflower seed. Middle: She waters it every day and a sprout appears. End: By summer the sunflower grew taller than Amara.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Leo was building a tower out of blocks. It fell down three times. Each time he tried again and made the base wider. On the fourth try the tower stood tall and did not fall.

What is the problem in this story? How is it solved?
items.answer: The problem is that Leo's tower keeps falling down. He solves it by making the base wider each time. On the fourth try the tower finally stands.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

A lion and a mouse became friends after the lion let the mouse go free. Later, the lion was caught in a net. He roared and struggled but could not get free. The mouse heard him and chewed through the ropes. The lion was free.

Is this story a fable, a folktale, or realistic fiction? How do you know?
items.answer: This is a fable. It has animal characters that act like people (a lion and a mouse who are friends), and it teaches a lesson about how even small creatures can help big ones.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Sofia forgot to bring her library book back on Friday. The library was closed on Saturday. On Monday, she returned it and paid the small fine. The librarian smiled and checked out a new book for her.

Describe the beginning, middle, and end of this story.
items.answer: Beginning: Sofia forgets to return her library book. Middle: The library is closed on Saturday so she cannot return it right away. End: She returns it on Monday, pays the fine, and gets a new book.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Long ago, a poor girl found a magic pot that cooked the best porridge in the world. She could not remember the magic word to make it stop. The porridge flowed out the door and down the street. At last she remembered the word, and the porridge stopped.

What kind of story is this — fable, folktale, or realistic fiction? How do you know?
items.answer: This is a folktale. It begins with 'Long ago,' has a magical object, and is set in a time that feels like long ago, not real life today. Realistic fiction does not have magic in it.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

James lost his homework on the way to school. He retraced his steps and found it on the sidewalk near the bus stop. He ran the rest of the way to school and turned it in just before class started.

How does the ending of this story conclude the action?
items.answer: The ending resolves the problem: James finds his homework and turns it in on time. The action is concluded because the homework is recovered and delivered.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Nadia's class went on a field trip to the nature center. First they learned about local birds. Then they walked a nature trail and saw a real hawk. At the end of the trip they each planted a wildflower seed to take home.

What does the beginning of this story introduce?
items.answer: The beginning introduces the setting (the nature center) and the characters (Nadia's class). It also introduces the first activity, learning about local birds, which starts the story.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Owen wanted a pet fish but his mom said he had to prove he was responsible first. She gave him a plant to water every day for a month. Owen watered the plant every single day. At the end of the month his mom took him to the pet store and he chose a blue betta fish.

What is the problem in this story? What does Owen do to solve it?
items.answer: The problem is that Owen wants a fish but has to prove he is responsible first. He solves the problem by watering the plant every day for a month without missing a day.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

A tortoise was very slow. All the other animals could run and jump and swim faster than she could. One day there was a long journey to make across the land. Most animals ran ahead but got tired and stopped to rest. The tortoise walked steadily all day. She arrived first.

Is this story a fable? What lesson does it teach?
items.answer: Yes, this is a fable. It has animal characters and teaches the lesson that slow, steady effort can beat rushing and stopping.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Amara's birthday was coming and she could not decide what to wish for when she blew out her candles. She thought about it all week. On the day of her birthday she still had not decided. When the moment came, she closed her eyes and wished for a good year for everyone in her family.

How does the beginning of this story introduce the conflict or problem?
items.answer: The beginning introduces Amara's conflict: she cannot decide what to wish for on her birthday. This is the problem that runs through the whole story.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Leo's team needed one more player for their kickball game. Leo asked a new student named Deshi if he wanted to play. Deshi said yes. He turned out to be the best kicker on the field, and Leo's team won.

Describe the beginning, middle, and end of this story in one sentence each.
items.answer: Beginning: Leo's kickball team needs one more player. Middle: Leo invites Deshi to join. End: Deshi turns out to be the best kicker and Leo's team wins.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Sofia and her dad were hiking when it started to rain. They did not have an umbrella, but they found a big tree and waited under it. After twenty minutes the rain stopped. They finished their hike in sunshine.

How does the middle of this story create a challenge, and how does the end resolve it?
items.answer: The middle creates a challenge by having it start raining without an umbrella available. The end resolves it by having the rain stop after twenty minutes, allowing them to finish the hike in sunshine.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Long ago a kind cobbler always left shoes outside his door for anyone who could not afford them. One winter, his own shoes wore out and he could not afford new leather. When he woke up the next morning, a pair of finished shoes sat on his workbench. His neighbors had made them while he slept.

What is the genre of this story? Describe the structural feature that makes the beginning and end mirror each other.
items.answer: This is a folktale (or fairy tale). The beginning shows the cobbler giving shoes to others. The ending mirrors this: his neighbors give shoes back to him. The giving in the beginning is returned at the end, creating a circular structure.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

James wanted to read a chapter book all by himself for the first time. He started on Monday and read a few pages each night. By Friday he had finished the whole book. He put it on his shelf and picked up another one.

What does the ending of this story tell you about James?
items.answer: The ending shows James successfully completed his first chapter book and immediately chose another one. It tells us he is proud of what he did and ready to keep reading.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Nadia found a stray dog. She wanted to keep it, but her apartment did not allow pets. She posted photos on neighborhood signs with her phone number. A week later, a family called — it was their dog, Pepper, who had escaped. They brought Nadia a gift basket to say thank you.

Is this story realistic fiction, a fable, or a folktale? How do you know?
items.answer: This is realistic fiction. The events, finding a stray dog, posting signs, and getting a phone call, could all happen in real life. There are no talking animals, magic, or 'long ago' setting.
